newsitem.title: USA: U.S. money managers more bullish on US debt-survey.
newsitem.headline: U.S. money managers more bullish on US debt-survey.

text.p: Money managers were more bullish on the U.S. debt markets over the past week, according to a survey by Stone & McCarthy Research Associates.

"While money managers have been more active in the market over the past several weeks than duration ratios alone would suggest, measured duration extension has been limited by mortgage exposure," the report said.
In the week ended July 29, the cash/assets ratio fell to 7.33 percent from 8.16 percent on an arithmetic basis and fell to 5.93 percent from 6.02 percent on a weighted basis.
The survey's actual/target duration index rose to 100.59 percent from 100.54 percent on an arithmetic basis and rose to 99.82 percent from 99.35 percent on a weighted basis.
Duration refers to a portfolio's average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
The survey's bear/bull index rose to 5.05 from 4.92 on an arithmetic basis. It rose to 4.71 from 4.53 on an asset-weighted basis.
A number above 5.00 is seen as indicating investors are mostly long on the market.
Seventeen percent of the portfolio managers surveyed said they were planning to be active in the coming week, up from 13 percent the week ending July 15.
The Stone & McCarthy survey is conducted by the research firm weekly. It includes 25 market participants with total assets of about $100 billion, the firm said.
* Table provided by Stone and McCarthy Research Associates.
** Respondents intending to adjust portfolio in coming week.
